anomalies.observed: The TPS62933 (U1) feedback divider is drawn with R14 = 5.23 kΩ between the +5 V/L1 output node and the FB pin, and R15 = 10 kΩ from FB to GND (Power Train block, sheet 1).
anomalies.expected: The TPS62933 uses a 0.8 V reference, so a 5 V output requires R_top/R_bottom = 5.25; with R15 = 10 kΩ the top resistor must be about 52.3 kΩ (the datasheet value for 5 V). 5.23 kΩ against 10 kΩ gives Vout = 0.8 × (1 + 0.523) ≈ 1.2 V (≈2.3 V even if the two resistors are transposed), which is far from the specified 5 V rail.

evidence.quote: U1 TPS62933 ... L1 10µH ... R14 5.23k ... R15 10k ... +5V (POWER TRAIN, sheet 1)
U1 — TPS62933 (TI) | 24 V → 5 V synchronous buck regulator, 3 A

anomalies.impact: The +5 V rail would regulate to roughly 1.2 V instead of 5 V; U2 (AZ1117-3.3) would be in dropout and the ESP32-C6 DevKit would not start, so the board would be effectively dead.

parsed.summary: One anomaly found: the 24 V→5 V buck (U1 TPS62933) feedback divider is mis-valued — R14 = 5.23 kΩ with R15 = 10 kΩ programs about 1.2 V instead of the specified 5 V, so the board could not power up. No other deviation from the specification was identified in the drawing.
